questions.stem: Which of the following describes the art of command that a company commander practices?
questions.key: It comprises authority, decision making, and leadership
distractors: It comprises command, control, and communication
It comprises authority, discipline, and obedience
It comprises leadership, management, and command
questions.explanation: The handout says the company commander practices the art of command, which comprises authority, decision making, and leadership.
why: Command, control and communication is not how the handout describes the art of command.
Discipline and obedience are not listed as its components.
Leadership, management and command are what commandership applies to authority, not the components of the art of command.

questions.stem: Which term describes applying not only leadership but also management and command, and applying these to authority, as a commander with duties and responsibilities to fulfil?
questions.explanation: Slide 16 (Foremost Commandership): commandership leads a commander to apply leadership, management and command to authority, with duties and responsibilities to fulfil.
why: Company administration is not the term the handout uses for applying leadership, management and command to authority.
Judicial responsibility is one of the company commander's responsibilities (enforcing the law, protecting rights), not this concept.
Troop leading is a procedure for planning and preparing operations, not this concept.

questions.stem: Which list contains the three foundations a company commander needs to develop for the leadership position?
questions.explanation: Because the CO is expected to be the unit standard, three foundations are developed: character, presence and intellect.
why: Honor, duty and patriotism are the Army core values embodied under character.
Competence and confidence appear as traits within presence and character, not as the three foundations.
Initiative is not one of the three foundations; character is missing.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a characteristic of a CO who is a person of intellect?
questions.explanation: Resilient is listed under a person of presence (fit, confident, resilient). Intellect lists mentally agile, sound judgement, innovative, tactful and expert.
why: Innovative is listed under intellect.
Tactful is listed under intellect.
Mentally agile is listed under intellect.

questions.stem: Which of the following defines the Training Responsibilities of a company commander?
questions.key: Training to fight to win is the number one priority and always the most important responsibility
distractors: Ensuring efficient processing of soldiers' personnel actions and establishing effective personnel management programs
Properly maintaining, securing, and accounting for unit property on unit records
Placing high importance on day-to-day, two-way communication with subordinates
questions.explanation: The handout states that training to fight to win is the company commander's number one priority and always the most important responsibility.
why: That is the Personnel and Administration responsibility.
That is the Supply responsibility.
That is part of the Interpersonal responsibility.

questions.stem: A company commander personally handles key property accountability issues, keeps track of inventories, and institutes a No Pilferage Policy. Which responsibility is being carried out?
questions.explanation: Handling key property accountability personally, tracking inventories and instituting a No Pilferage Policy are listed under Supply Responsibilities.
why: Personnel and administration deals with personnel actions, reports and awards.
Training responsibilities deal with training philosophy, METL and sustainment training.
Combat responsibilities deal with planning, proficiency and modeling leader development.

questions.stem: A company commander makes sure his troops understand the Codes of Conduct/Ethics and bases the unit's standards of discipline on military laws and regulations. Which responsibility does this describe?
questions.explanation: Enforcing the law and basing discipline standards on military laws and regulations, together with protecting soldiers' rights, fall under Judicial Responsibilities.
why: Interpersonal responsibilities concern counselling, coaching, mentoring and two-way communication.
Personnel and administration concern processing personnel actions and awards.
Combat responsibilities concern planning, skills and modeling leader development.

questions.stem: A company commander gets to know his subordinate leaders, acts as counsellor, coach and mentor, and is a role model in conduct, appearance and finances. Which responsibility does this describe?
questions.explanation: Knowing your role as counsellor, coach and mentor, knowing subordinate leaders and being a role model are listed under Interpersonal Responsibilities.
why: Judicial responsibilities concern punishment decisions and soldiers' rights.
Supply responsibilities concern property accountability.
Training responsibilities concern METL and performance-oriented training.

questions.stem: It means demonstrating your leadership by going first.
questions.explanation: The handout says that leading from the front means that you demonstrate your leadership by going first.
why: Being decisive means valuing time, the most valuable resource.
Fostering teamwork builds a cohesive unit moving toward a common goal.
Being aggressive and bold refers to dedication, energy and direction.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT part of the FIRST that a company commander needs for successful commandership?
questions.explanation: FIRST stands for Faith, Increase knowledge, reliable C3 system, positive Staff relationships and Time management system. Being fit and energetic is a separate principle.
why: Faith is the F in FIRST.
Time management system is the T in FIRST.
A reliable C3 system is the R in FIRST.

questions.stem: It is the courage to take action for moral reasons despite the risk of adverse consequences.
questions.explanation: The handout defines moral courage as the courage to take action for moral reasons despite the risk of adverse consequences.
why: Physical courage is overcoming fear of physical danger.
Self-confidence is thinking positively about the future and willingness to take necessary risks.
Sheer determination is persevering toward a difficult goal despite obstacles.

questions.stem: A company commander names an intelligence team when necessary, limits information to those who need it, and evaluates the information gathered. Which functional role is being performed?
questions.explanation: These actions come from the INTELLIGENCE keys to effectiveness: name an intelligence team, limit information to those with need, and evaluate information gathered.
why: The operations officer keys concern supervising tasks and planning and executing operations.
The logistics officer keys concern property, maintenance and inventory.
The personnel officer keys concern records, morale programs and personnel actions.
